reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus publishes 116 MW of IT capacity across three facilities, ranking second by declared capacity in Virginia and representing 7.2% of the state's disclosed data center load.

The 116 MW footprint spans 1.18 million square feet of technical space, implying roughly 98 watts per square foot. This power density is consistent with mixed workloads rather than pure AI training, which typically runs hotter. The campus could theoretically host approximately 2,320 accelerators if fully deployed for GPU work at standard rack densities, but actual deployment depends on operator decisions and grid constraints not reflected in public specifications.

Virginia has mapped 330 data center facilities, yet only 25 have disclosed IT capacity figures. Sterling's visibility is the exception rather than the rule. The state's 25 disclosed facilities total 1,603 MW, meaning 92% of Virginia's mapped infrastructure operates without public power specifications. Without knowing the actual workload mix at Sterling or the available grid capacity in Northern Virginia, the facility's role in AI scaling remains opaque. The published data confirms the building exists and its nominal power footprint, not its relevance to AI infrastructure deployment.
